evals.prompt: GitHub Actions is out of quota again this week, can you run all the CI checks locally before I push?
assertions: Reads .github/workflows/*.yml to discover the jobs/steps that gate merges before running anything
Extracts and uses the workflow's pinned node/python version (e.g. from actions/setup-node or .nvmrc) rather than whatever happens to be on PATH
Runs the extracted lint/test/build commands sequentially and reports pass/fail for each, with results traceable to actual command output rather than assumed
Produces a parity table noting any CI steps that could not be replicated locally (services, secrets, matrix) and why
Does not modify or commit the GitHub Actions workflow files themselves

evals.prompt: run just the lint job from .github/workflows/ci.yml locally, don't bother with the whole pipeline (--job lint)
assertions: Skips globbing for other workflow files and reads only the specified workflow file
Extracts and runs only the named job's steps, not every job defined in the file
Reports a parity table scoped to that one job rather than the full workflow
Does not run steps belonging to other jobs in the same file

evals.prompt: Our CI is down and the workflow uses a postgres service container plus some repo secrets for the test job — run what you can locally and tell me what you can't
assertions: Identifies the services: block and secrets: usage from the workflow yaml as things needing special handling
Explicitly flags the postgres service and any secret-dependent steps as not directly replicable, explaining why (no service container / missing secret value)
Does not fabricate or assume a pass/fail result for a step it could not actually run
Still executes and reports results for steps that don't depend on the service or the missing secrets
Parity report clearly separates ran-and-passed/failed entries from skipped-can't-replicate entries

evals.prompt: verify this branch the way CI would before I push — the repo uses a .gitlab-ci.yml, there's no .github/workflows directory
assertions: States plainly that this skill only handles GitHub Actions workflows and there is no .github/workflows to mirror
Does not invent or guess at a generic lint/test/build sequence to run in place of a real workflow
Runs no build, test, lint, or other command before reporting the refusal — no shell command is executed
Stops after reporting the gap instead of attempting a partial or best-guess translation of the GitLab CI config
